title: The Bank Loan a Mother Took Out for the First Cardiopad
conflicts: Units sold: April 2016 Zang said 43 kits (Camer.be), Africanews said 47; 1 June 2016 TIC Mag said about 300 assembled with no Cameroonian public-hospital order; 6 June 2016 CNN reported Zang saying he had sold hundreds; Dec 2016 National Geographic said nearly 70; Jan 2017 Business in Cameroon said 'officially about 300 kits were sold in 2016'; 2021 Himore said 267 Cameroonian health centres. The story gives the 2016 figures with speaker and date and the 2021 figure as the company's own, leaning on none. Also: first batch 20 devices (Zang 2014) vs 30 (NatGeo 2016); government money $30,000 (Zang) vs about 30,000 euros (WIPO), both given; how he reached the president (video/social media in 2014, a journalist's article in 2016), story uses only the video account as his.
notes: Slate funding 'bootstrapped' changed to 'mixed' (mother's bank loan, then government grant and prizes). This is my one talQen edition. Quote is Tagore's Sadhana on statistics fixing what is in motion, applied by analogy (stance complicates).
